subject: Private deployment: operational escrow onboarding and redlines
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Park <natalie.park@crescenthealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment: operational escrow onboarding and redlines

Natalie —

Thanks for the call this morning. Per Crescent's procurement checklist, I wanted to summarize our suggested path for the private/VPC deployment redlines so legal and procurement can align on the same plan before we exchange marked documents. Key points we propose: 

- License boundary: customer holds runtime residency in their VPC; Redwood retains model artifacts and image signing controls. We can provide a signed verification artifact each release.
- Evidence window: offer a narrow, observer-only 4-hour evidence window for a one-time witness per release candidate (no interactive operator access).
- Snapshot custody: encrypted VM snapshot with customer-provided KMS key; Redwood to provide sealed proof-of-creation and HSM log excerpts.
- Operator console: provide a temporary, limited-scope console token scoped to diagnostics (no model weights, read-only perf metrics) for a single scheduled session.

Attached is Crescent's requirements doc you shared and a short draft MAP that maps responsibilities and timing. Can Laura and Marissa weigh in on any legal/contract risks here? If this plan looks acceptable we will prepare a single redline file (MSA + Order Form) for Crescent to review.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Redwood prepares redline bundle and an appendix explaining the evidence artifacts (2 business days).
2) Crescent confirms witness timing and procurement gating items (PO + SOC2 letter).
3) DocuSign exchange for the Order Form, followed by scheduling of the evidence session.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Attachment: Crescent_Requirements_20270411.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

From: Natalie Park <natalie.park@crescenthealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Crescent Health Procurement <procurement@crescenthealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: operational escrow onboarding and redlines

Jordan —

Appreciate the summary and the suggested MAP. Procurement has a few clarifying asks before legal engages: 

1) The 4-hour witness window — procurement needs to confirm whether that's per major release or per deployment. Our preference is one witness per major release plus an annually scheduled witnessing session.
2) For the snapshot custody, we require proof of destruction of any intermediate unencrypted artifacts and an attestation that Redwood personnel do not retain key escrow access unless explicitly granted through a documented procedure.
3) Can you provide a template SOC 2 attestation and two vendor references (preferably other healthcare customers) we can call?

I am attaching our internal requirements doc (high-level) so your legal team can see the procurement gating items.

If you can provide redlines by EOD Tuesday, procurement will aim to confirm the PO timeline on Wednesday.

— Natalie
Natalie Park
Senior Manager, Procurement | Crescent Health
Attachment: Crescent_InternalReqs_20270411.pdf (PDF, 180KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Park <natalie.park@crescenthealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: operational escrow onboarding and redlines

Natalie —

Thanks — we can accommodate procurement's asks with a few clarifications: 

- Witness cadence: we'll commit to one witness session per major release (major defined in Order Form Annex) and an annual witness for governance purposes. We will add language to the annex to reflect this cadence and the scheduling SLA (45 days notice).
- Snapshot custody: Redwood will accept a requirement to use customer-provided KMS keys and will include an attestation clause that no Redwood engineer will retain unencrypted copies. We'll include a destruction certification that is timestamped and signed by an authorized Redwood operations lead.
- SOC 2: attached is our SOC 2 Type II letter (redacted) and two healthcare references (contact names + phone).

I'll attach our initial redlines (MSA + Order Form) and a short appendix that explains the artifact types (sealed snapshot hash, HSM audit excerpt, console token expiration policy). If Laura or Marissa want different wording I can iterate quickly.

Attached: redlines_marked.docx (MS Word, tracked changes)

Jordan

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Park <natalie.park@crescenthealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: operational escrow onboarding and redlines

Natalie / Jordan / Marissa —

I reviewed Jordan's draft redlines. High level notes for Crescent's counsel: 

1) MSA Annex: we will add a narrow operational annex (Annex C) that defines evidence artifacts, witness cadence, and the limited console token scope. Language will be explicit that the console token provides diagnostics-only access and is time-boxed.
2) Order Form: we will include the customer-provided KMS key clause and a short attestation template for destruction of intermediate artifacts. We recommend a single-line clause for indemnity carve-outs limited to misuse of customer keys.
3) Escrow-lite: instead of a full source-code escrow, propose an "escrow-lite" exhibit that provides sealed runtime images + signed manifests under controlled witness conditions — this reduces IP exposure while delivering verifiable proofs.

I have attached a PDF of the MSA with track changes for Crescent counsel to review. Main items that will likely be negotiated: witness scheduling SLA, list of accepted evidence artifacts, and the liability carve-out language.

If Crescent wants, we can prepare a short one-page exhibit explaining the technical artifacts (non-legal) to attach to the MSA — often that helps procurement and engineers align.

— Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference
Attachment: msa_track_changes.pdf (PDF, 95KB)

From: Natalie Park <natalie.park@crescenthealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@crescenthealth.com>, Crescent Health Procurement <procurement@crescenthealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: operational escrow onboarding and redlines

Laura / Jordan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the marked MSA. Procurement reviewed the changes and Crescent legal is okay with the "escrow-lite" approach as long as the annex includes:

- A definitive list of artifact types that are acceptable for proof (sealed snapshot hash, signed runtime manifest, HSM audit extract).
- A documented procedure for scheduling the witness session with a 45-day SLA and one backup date.
- The destruction attestation must include a timestamp and the name/title of the Redwood signatory.

Procurement will provide PO terms pending a final DocuSign exchange for the Order Form. Could you send the DocuSign link for the Order Form and MSA bundle and an expected schedule for the evidence session? Procurement would like the session to occur within 15 business days after signature, if possible.

I'll loop in our technical lead if we need to drill into artifact formats.

— Natalie
Senior Manager, Procurement | Crescent Health
